doc.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020

title: Making the concert video during the pandemic
summary: Harris explains using the video format and camera cuts instead of recreating a live show.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well this has been a fascinating conversation. Thanks, Michelle for setting it up and again, the video you provided us with is really wonderful. I can’t wait to see the complete program and that someday down the road we’ll see you in person.

And I want to add one thing about the video process, much like the process of creating music. You never want to try to recreate something. That’s sort of a losing battle. Charlie Parker was really good. He did a great job of documenting the world that he inhabited. So when I tried to figure out well what’s the next step given this pandemic I said well let’s not try to recreate a live experience. But what we want to do is take a look at the format that we’re utilizing and look at the assets of that format and highlight those. So I think what was really exciting was we took a lot of time to prepare was utilizing video editing. So when you’re live you’re sitting in one space in a concert hall, there’s so much going on that you can’t think. But you have one perspective. So we focused a lot on cutting camera angles right at the moment when something interesting happened in the music so you hear it and you get a visual cue. But the experience is totally different than live. But I © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

find it to be really different — I find it to be really insightful. I learned more about what’s happening in the music as a viewer in the video platform than I do live. When it’s live I feel more the whole thing. But in this someone doing something interesting, and an attack over there and things that I wouldn’t always catch.

Yeah. There was a couple of moments where people’s expressions were so in tune with some sound that happened. That’s like great. You know, that look that musicians get. And to capture that that’s way cool.
